situation:
You are the channel marketing manager at WINDROW SPORTS MUSEUM AND HALL OF FAME, which has drawn visitors to its exhibits and its induction ceremonies for more than forty years. The vice president of marketing (judge) has asked you to recommend how the museum will sell and distribute admission for the coming quarter, and what happens to the sponsor activation that sits in the middle of it.

WINDROW sells admission two ways. Its own box office and website keep the buyer's contact information and the membership renewal with the museum. VISTAPASS, a regional attractions pass, sells the museum inside a bundle and keeps the buyer's information itself. ARCADIA SPORTS EXPERIENCE, an interactive attraction that opened across the river last year, has taken a growing share of the family visits WINDROW once counted on.

KILNBROOK WIRELESS, the museum's title sponsor, funds a quarter of the exhibit budget, and its activation requires visitors to download the sponsor's app and check in at kiosks in the main hall before the advertised discount applies. Visitors dislike it. The kiosk lines back up into the ticketing area, and the museum's own comment cards name the check-in more often than any exhibit in the building.

Moving the discounted admission onto VISTAPASS would fill the galleries this quarter, and it hands the buyer's contact information and the renewal relationship to the pass operator, so direct box office sales and membership renewals fall next quarter. Keeping admission on the museum's own box office and website and rebuilding the sponsor's check-in into a staffed greeting at the door protects those renewals, and it leaves attendance flat this quarter while ARCADIA SPORTS EXPERIENCE takes share.

The vice president of marketing (judge) wants your recommendation on which channels carry admission for the quarter, how that choice fits the promotion and membership work already booked, and how the front-of-house staff will be told what is changing. The vice president of marketing (judge) will greet you, hear your ideas and ask questions. When you have finished answering, the vice president of marketing (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of vice president of marketing (judge) at WINDROW SPORTS MUSEUM AND HALL OF FAME.

Business background is the same as the situation above. Admission moves through the museum's own box office and website or through the VISTAPASS bundle, the title sponsor funds a quarter of the exhibit budget and requires the app check-in at the kiosks, and ARCADIA SPORTS EXPERIENCE is taking family visits the museum used to hold.

You have asked the channel marketing manager (participant) to recommend which channels carry admission for the coming quarter, what happens to the sponsor's activation, and how the front-of-house staff hear about the change.

During the course of the role-play you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: What is the first change you would make, and who would make it?
How would you tell the front-of-house staff what is changing?
